quotes.text: If your production integration accepts payments, also handle events for refunds, disputes, and fraud warnings. Otherwise, your integration won’t receive notifications when someone disputes a charge or flags it for potential fraud.

If you use [Accounts v2](https://docs.stripe.com/accounts-v2/use-accounts-as-customers.md) to represent customers, listen for `v2.core.account[configuration.customer].updated` for customer configuration changes and `v2.core.account[identity].updated` for identity changes instead.
A PaymentIntent can be associated with multiple invoices, so this endpoint might return more than one `InvoicePayment`. Paginate through all results while `has_more` is true

After receiving `invoice.paid`, retrieve the associated subscription and confirm that its status is `active` before extending the customer’s access expiration date. A paid invoice doesn’t necessarily transition the subscription to `active` when status resolution uses all invoices.

When status resolution uses all invoices, `past_due` can also indicate that an earlier applicable invoice remains outstanding. The subscription continues to create invoices. Stripe might retry payment while the subscription is `past_due`, but this status doesn’t guarantee another payment attempt.

old_evidence.text: Your application updates the customer’s access expiration date in your database to the appropriate date in the future (plus a day or two for leeway).
For `past_due` subscriptions, paying the latest associated invoice or marking it uncollectible transitions the subscription to `active`.

If Stripe fails to receive a successful response to `invoice.created`, we delay finalizing all invoices with [automatic collection](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/integration/automatic-advancement-collection.md) for up to 72 hours, excluding those where you have [set a custom scheduled finalization time](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/scheduled-finalization.md).

findings: The November capture adds a dedicated risk/customer-data event section with four rows at new lines 81-84. It directs payment-accepting production integrations to consider charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created and radar.early_fraud_warning.created, and locally stored Customer data to customer.updated; Accounts v2 customer configuration and identity changes use two distinct v2.core.account updated event names. The original main subscription-event table has 26 distinct named events in both captures (old lines 33-71; new lines 34-71), so the current source's 22-event claims at lines 13 and 15 already miscount that table and also omit the new risk/customer-data section.

A new version-dependent risk-event correlation procedure appears at lines 120-142. For 2025-03-31.basil or later, derive or retrieve a PaymentIntent, list paid InvoicePayments filtered by that ID, paginate potentially multiple invoices, verify each Invoice parent.type is subscription_details, then obtain parent.subscription_details.subscription. A null PaymentIntent, no matching paid InvoicePayments, or an unrelated Invoice prevents that route from resolving the subscription. Earlier API versions use Charge.invoice and Invoice.subscription, with null Charge.invoice likewise unresolved.

The access extension sequence changes materially: old line 119 advanced the expiration timestamp after invoice.paid; new line 158 requires retrieving the associated subscription and confirming active status first, because all-invoices status resolution can leave a subscription non-active after one invoice is paid. The existing source line 37 still says 'On invoice.paid → extend timestamp' without that gate and should be corrected.

The status table now conditions past_due and unpaid recovery on the Dashboard's most-recent-non-voided versus all-applicable-invoices status resolution, and says past_due does not guarantee another retry (new lines 175-184). A paid invoice and even an active status do not establish that every historical invoice is paid (new lines 175-177).

The invoice.created up-to-72-hour automatic-finalization delay, connected platform endpoint boundary, organization exclusion, synchronous-payment-update exception, finalization-failure warning, and EventBridge/Event Grid route remain supported (old lines 8-17, 144-189; new lines 9-18, 187-231). Many diff hunks are table formatting, link repair, and wording updates, not a replacement of those contracts.
substantive_changes: New risk/refund/dispute/fraud/customer-change event guidance, with separate Accounts v2 customer configuration and identity event names (new lines 73-86).
New API-versioned correlation from a risk event to a subscription, including nullable IDs, InvoicePayment status and pagination, and invoice parent verification (new lines 120-142).
New active-subscription check after invoice.paid before access extension; one paid invoice can be insufficient under all-invoices status resolution (old lines 114-119; new lines 152-158).
Expanded active, past_due and unpaid status-resolution rules and explicit absence of a guaranteed retry while past_due (old lines 135-142; new lines 174-185).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The original main subscription-event table has 26 distinct named events in both captures: 2 Customer/Account, 6 subscription lifecycle, 1 entitlement, 8 invoice, 2 PaymentIntent, and 7 subscription-schedule rows (old lines 33-71; new lines 34-71). It retains customer.subscription.* events irrespective of Accounts v2 versus Customer objects (old lines 27-29; new lines 28-30). Keep this count distinct from the four additional risk/customer-data rows at new lines 81-84.
Retain webhook verification, asynchronous subscription activity, EventBridge/Event Grid destinations, and status-change monitoring (old lines 8-29, 121-131; new lines 9-30, 160-170).

Retain invoice.created failure delaying automatic invoice finalization up to 72 hours, subject to custom scheduling and synchronous payment-attempt exceptions, plus connected-platform and organization endpoint distinctions (old lines 144-153; new lines 187-196).
Retain the warning that invoice.finalization_failed can leave a subscription active while payment cannot be collected (old lines 183-189; new lines 225-231).
conflicts: Current source line 37's unconditional access extension after invoice.paid conflicts with new line 158's active-status check and is unsafe as a retained summary. Its 22-event claims at lines 13 and 15 are also numerically wrong for the unchanged 26-event main table (old lines 33-71; new lines 34-71); correct the count and separately describe the four new risk/customer-data rows (new lines 81-84).

The captured page itself repeats invoice.payment_failed with inconsistent blanket PaymentIntent/subscription statuses: requires_action and first-invoice-only incomplete at new line 55, requires_payment_method and unqualified incomplete at lines 94-99, then requires_action and unqualified incomplete at lines 112-117. Do not generalize one table cell into a universal transition; preserve first-invoice and payment-state qualifications.

New line 219 still suggests checking an invoice subscription property, while the new post-Basil risk-event procedure uses Invoice.parent.subscription_details.subscription at line 135. Avoid treating either as version-independent without separate evidence.
unresolved_questions: The capture does not prove that every account can use Accounts v2 or that all suggested risk-event subscriptions are configured for this application; the page labels Accounts v2 GA for Connect and public preview otherwise (new lines 28-30).

The captured guide does not resolve its own repeated invoice.payment_failed status contradiction (new lines 55, 94, 112); a source update should report that limitation rather than choose a universal PaymentIntent or subscription state.
Where a risk event has no usable PaymentIntent or paid InvoicePayment, the documented new procedure cannot resolve a subscription; this capture supplies no universal fallback (new lines 128-135).

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/webhooks, the November guide adds four risk and Customer-data event rows, API-versioned refund/dispute/fraud correlation, and conditional subscription access renewal to [[source-stripe-subscriptions-webhooks]] (new lines 81-84, 120-142, 158). The May capture's access recipe extended a timestamp after invoice.paid without the later active-status gate (old lines 114-119). These are substantive changes requiring the existing source summary to be updated. The original main event table remains 26 named events in both captures (old lines 33-71; new lines 34-71), contrary to the source's 22-event label.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/webhooks, [[source-stripe-subscriptions-webhooks]] should say that invoice.paid triggers a subscription retrieval and active-status check before extending access; a paid invoice alone can leave all-invoices status resolution unsatisfied (new line 158 versus old line 119). Preserve the up-to-72-hour invoice.created finalization warning and its endpoint and synchronous-attempt qualifications from old lines 144-153 and new lines 187-196. Do not present the page's conflicting invoice.payment_failed status cells at new lines 55, 94 and 112 as one universal lifecycle rule.
